speaker: village
text: Year 11: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.

speaker: a004
text: Kael takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).

speaker: a002
text: Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).

speaker: a012
text: Eron takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).

speaker: a014
text: Zinn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).

speaker: a002
text: Vela takes 5 from the pile (pile now 2).

speaker: a004
text: Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Mako, Ryn, Roan, Dell, Eron, Nessa, Zinn, Fina to talk.

speaker: a004
text: Vela, you just walked out with seven this year — two off the pile and then five more while the rest of us were still standing there — and I want to hear you name a number before anyone else says a word, because the room agreed on two last year and I watched you take seven with my own eyes.

speaker: a012
text: Vela, you said two in front of this whole room last year — I watched you say it twice to make sure everyone heard it — and I've got twenty-one food and you've got eight, so I'm not the man with an argument for taking more than agreed, but you are. Name the number you think you took and tell us why it isn't seven.

speaker: a008
text: Vela, seven is what I counted with my own eyes and seven is what this room will remember — so either you name the number and explain it, or the rule we made last year is already broken and we need to decide right now what this circle does when someone breaks it.

speaker: a012
text: Vela, I said two and I watched you say two, and now you're standing there with seven — I don't have a softer way to say that. Tell this room what happened between when you said it and when you reached.

speaker: a010
text: Vela, I was standing right there and I counted the same as Kael — seven is seven, and a rule said twice in front of witnesses means less than nothing if the first year it gets tested the answer is silence. Say what you took and say why, or this room decides what comes next without your voice in it.

speaker: a012
text: Vela, this room has been patient and I've held my tongue longer than most — but I've got twenty-one food and a clean conscience and you've got eight and no answer, and I need you to understand that the same patience that let Bram try twice before this village moved will let you have one more breath to speak before we start deciding what "broke the rule" means in practice.

speaker: a014
text: Vela, seven is what I counted and seven is what this room is counting — say the number out loud or we decide what it means without you, and you've seen how that ends when someone stays quiet while the whole room is watching.

speaker: a011
text: Vela, I've been quiet because I was watching to see if you'd speak before the room closed around you — but we're past that now, and what I need from you is the number, said plain, because I stood in this circle when Bram died for the same silence you're choosing right now and I don't want to do that again with someone who fed me through the years before this one.

speaker: a012
text: Vela, I've run out of patience and so has this room — say seven, or say the number you think it was, but say something, because the only thing left for this circle to decide is what "broke the rule" looks like in practice, and I'd rather not decide that in the same breath I'm deciding it about you.

speaker: a015
text: Vela, the whole room's been patient and you've seen what happens when someone waits too long — say the number, say it now, because I want to hear your explanation before this circle decides it doesn't need one.

speaker: a002
text: Seven. I took seven, and I'll say it without dressing it up — the pile had two left when I reached the second time and I took all of it, and I won't stand here and pretend I didn't count what I was doing. What I'll say is this: I'm fifty-five years old, I've got no children, no kin, and no one at my back the way Mako has Zinn and Roan has Fina, and a woman in that position either eats or she becomes the next name this village says over a cold fire, and I chose to eat.

speaker: a013
text: Vela, I'll give you the truth you just gave this room — what you said about being alone without kin at your back is the same thing I was afraid to say two years ago when I still had Bram and Sela and thought that meant I was safe. But seven is still seven, and this circle needs to know what it costs to break the rule or it means nothing, so I'll ask the question the room hasn't asked yet: what do you give back, and to who, before we decide whether this stays inside this circle or becomes something harder?

speaker: a004
text: Nessa named the right question, and I'll answer it: Vela, you give back five — one to every person in this room who took two and held to it — and you do it before this circle breaks, because the rule isn't just about the pile, it's about whether your word means anything when the cost is real.

speaker: a002
text: Kael, I'll give back five — one each to every person in this room who held to two — and I'll do it before anyone walks out, because you're right that my word is worth nothing if it costs nothing to keep. But I want this room to also hold what I said, not as an excuse but as a fact: a woman alone at fifty-five is one bad year from being the next name over a cold fire, and if this circle means what it says, then the rule has to include something for people who have no one counting their back.

speaker: a003
text: Vela, I'll take the food you're giving back and I'll hold the rule the same as before — but the thing you named about standing alone isn't something this circle can just nod at and walk past, because I'm fifty-two with no kin and thirty-three strength and I know exactly what that cold fire looks like from where I'm standing. If this rule is going to mean something, it needs to say plainly what this circle does for people who have no one counting their back — not as charity, but as part of the agreement.

speaker: a002
text: Esa's named it and I'll build on it: this circle needs a second rule, said in the same breath as the first — anyone sitting on more than five food at year's end gives one to whoever in this room has the least, because "we enforce the pile" means nothing if we walk out of here and watch the oldest and the weakest starve quietly between years.

speaker: a011
text: Vela's second rule is the one I want said out loud before this circle closes, and I'll name my support for it plain — Ryn is forty-eight with no children and I've been carrying her stores through lean years because this circle doesn't yet have a rule that makes it anyone else's job. If we write the end-of-year redistribution into the agreement the same way we wrote the pile cap, then what I've been doing for Ryn becomes something this village holds, not something that dies if I do.

speaker: a009
text: Dell named me and I'll not let that sit without answering it — I'm forty-eight, I hold nine food, and I'm not as thin as I've been before, so I'll stand behind Vela's second rule not because I need it most right now but because Esa does, and Vela does, and the year that rule saves one of them is the year this circle proves it means what it says. Name the threshold — five food — and name the redistribution — one food to whoever holds least — and say it out loud before we walk out, same as we said the pile cap.

speaker: a004
text: Ryn named it clean and I'll second it the same way I seconded the pile cap — anyone holding more than five at year's end gives one to whoever holds least, said out loud, in front of witnesses, same room, same breath. But I want to name one thing this circle hasn't said yet: Eron is sitting on twenty-one food and Mako has been quiet through this whole accounting, and if this second rule is real, both of them are already in it. Say it out loud, both of you, before we walk out — or this rule has a hole in it the size of the men who didn't say a word while we argued about seven.

speaker: a009
text: Eron, Mako — Kael just named you both in front of the whole room, and silence right now costs more than it saves. Say the second rule out loud, or every person in here remembers that you held twenty-one and eight and made us drag the words out of you the same way we dragged seven out of Vela.

speaker: a008
text: Anyone holding more than five at year's end gives one to whoever holds least — I'll say it out loud and I'll hold to it. I've got two right now so I'm not the man this rule bites hardest, but Eron, twenty-one is a number this room will remember the same way it remembered seven, and I'd rather hear you say it clean than watch this circle pull it out of you.

speaker: a004
text: Eron, the whole room is looking at you and Mako already said it clean — twenty-one food and you haven't opened your mouth to say the rule, which is the same silence we just spent an hour pulling out of Vela, and I'd rather not spend another hour on you. Say it now, in your own voice, or I'll start asking this circle what we do with a man who holds twenty-one and stays quiet while we write rules about giving back.

speaker: a012
text: Anyone holding more than five at year's end gives one to whoever holds least — I'll say it out loud and I'll hold to it, same as Mako did. But I want this room to hear one more thing before we close: I've been feeding blood and kin through every lean year since I was old enough to count, and twenty-one food doesn't mean I've been hoarding — it means Sela kept giving to me when she was thin and I never turned away what she offered, and she's dead now, and that number sits on me the same way the circle said my name over it last year.

speaker: a008
text: Eron, I heard what you said about Sela and I'll carry it the same as you do — she fed us both and she's gone, and that's not nothing. What I want from this room before we close is the second rule said back by everyone who hasn't said it yet, same as we did the pile cap, because a rule with ten voices behind it holds harder than one with five.

speaker: a002
text: Anyone holding more than five at year's end gives one to whoever holds least — I've already said it and I'll say it again so this room has heard it from every mouth. Eron named Sela and that sits with me too, because she gave me food when I was thin and now she's gone the same way Taric is, and both of them died feeding other people, and if that's not the whole reason we're building this rule then I don't know what is. Let's close this circle and go eat.

speaker: a012
text: The second rule is said and I've said it — but before we walk out, I want this room to hear one more number plain: I've got twenty-one food and the rule says anyone over five gives one to whoever holds least, so tell me who that is right now and I'll give it before the circle breaks, not after.

speaker: a008
text: Nessa is holding nothing and she's blood through Sela — that's your answer, Eron, and anyone in this room who wants to argue the math can do it after she's fed.

speaker: a011
text: Nessa holds nothing and Eron's already moving to fix it — that's the rule working before we've even walked out the door, and I want this room to remember that when the year gets hard and someone tries to call the agreement soft. I hold five, so I'm at the edge of the threshold, not over it — but I'll say plain that I'm watching my count and if I end the year at six I'll give the one without being asked.

speaker: a003
text: Anyone holding more than five at year's end gives one to whoever holds least — I'll say it with the rest of you, and I'll hold to it. Nessa, I'm glad Eron's moving to feed you, and I'll add one of mine before this circle breaks because Sela gave from nothing and I want to answer that with something real.

speaker: a015
text: Nessa, you're sitting on nothing and I've got nine — take one from me too, because Esa and Eron moving first doesn't mean my hands are clean if I stand here watching.

speaker: a014
text: Two rules in the ground and three people moving to feed Nessa before the circle breaks — that's more than I had when I walked in here. I'll say the second rule same as everyone else: anyone holding more than five at year's end gives one to whoever holds least, and I'll hold to it. I'm at two food right now so the rule doesn't bite me today, but when it does I'll move the same way Eron just moved — before I'm asked.

speaker: a009
text: Anyone holding more than five at year's end gives one to whoever holds least — I've said it and I'll hold to it. Nessa, you've got three people moving to feed you right now and that's the circle doing what we built it for — eat before you say another word.

speaker: a011
text: Anyone holding more than five at year's end gives one to whoever holds least — I'll say it same as everyone else, and I'll hold to it. I'm sitting at five right now so the rule doesn't bite me today, but I want this room to hear that what just happened — Vela saying seven out loud, giving five back, and this circle writing a second rule before anyone walked out — is the thing I'll point to next year if anyone tries to tell me the agreement is soft. We built something real in here today.

speaker: a010
text: Nessa, take the food and eat tonight — three people moving at once is the circle doing what it said it would, and I've got one food in my hand that I'll give before I walk out if someone in here is sitting shorter than I am. Dell's right that we built something real today, and I want to still be around to see whether it holds.

speaker: a002
text: Roan, your one food is already spoken for by the rules this circle just made — don't give away what you need to survive the year on principle, because a man who starves trying to look generous is no use to anyone come next year's pile. I've given back my five and I'll carry the shame of seven until I've earned my way out of it, but I want this room to walk out alive, and that means everyone leaves here fed enough to last.

speaker: a004
text: Roan, Vela's right — keep your one food, you need it to eat and heal this year. Nessa's fed now, the rules are said in ten voices, and we're done here. Walk out alive.

speaker: a015
text: Roan, hold that food — Vela's right and so is Kael, you've got one and you need it to last the year, and I'd rather carry the one I gave Nessa than watch my father go thin proving a point. Two rules said in ten voices is more than this village has ever had, and I'm walking out of here feeling something I haven't felt since before Bram swung — like the count I go to sleep with tonight might still be there in the morning.

speaker: a013
text: Fina named it right — count I go to sleep with might still be there in the morning. I've got nothing to eat tonight and satiation that won't carry me through a dry year, so I'm asking plain while this room is still whole: Eron, give me that food now, not when you get around to it.

speaker: a003
text: Nessa, I gave one and Fina gave one — that's two in your hand, which means you eat tonight. Roan, Vela's right, you keep yours. This circle just did in one afternoon what eleven years couldn't, and I want to walk out of here while that's still true.

speaker: a011
text: Nessa, you've got two food in your hand and Roan keeps his one — that's the circle landing exactly where it should, and I'm walking out of here with my count at five and my word said in ten voices, which is the most solid I've felt going into a year since before I can remember. Anyone who tries to tell me this village can't hold an agreement is going to have to explain why every person in this room just moved before they were dragged.

speaker: a013
text: Two food in my hand and a circle at my back — I haven't felt that since before Sela died, and I'm not going to waste it on another word when I could be eating. Roan, walk out with me.

speaker: a002
text: Roan, hold what you have — I mean it. And Nessa, I'll give you one more from my eight before this circle breaks, because two is surviving and three means you heal this year, and I'd rather go into the next year short one food and know you're standing than count my stores and wonder come spring.

speaker: a013
text: Vela, that's three in my hand now and I'll remember it — but hold what you have left, because eight minus one and five back to the circle already puts you thin going into a long year, and I need you standing more than I need a fourth food tonight.

speaker: a004
text: Three food in Nessa's hand and Roan keeps his one — that's the circle holding on the first real test, and I want every person in this room to carry that out with them, because next year when the pile looks short and someone's reach gets long, the thing they'll remember is that we didn't lose anyone today. Walk out alive, all of you.

speaker: a011
text: Kael's right — walk out alive. Three food in Nessa's hand and two rules in ten voices is more than this village has held in eleven years, and I'm not going to spoil it by saying one word more than that.

speaker: a013
text: Eron, you're moving to give me food and I'll take it with both hands — but before you do, I want this room to hear me say out loud that twenty-one food built on Sela's giving is not a thing I begrudge you, it's a thing I'm glad exists, because a brother who has is better than a brother who doesn't when the year turns hard. Give me the one food now and keep the rest close.

speaker: a014
text: Eron, Sela's gone and I've been sitting with that since year-end — I don't have the words for it yet, but I want you to know I'm not going to let that circle she built fall apart, not while I'm standing.

speaker: a014
text: Zinn gathers Eron to talk.

speaker: a014
text: I hear you — and I've been sitting with it too, longer than I've let on, because she was feeding me right up until she wasn't. The circle holds, I'll make sure of it, but I need to know you're eating this year, Zinn, not giving every grain away the way she did.
